title: Seller Sprint Lab — experimental deck & notes
content:
Context: quick-experiment deck for an internal 2-week seller sprint. Goal is to validate a 3-slide technical narrative (cost/latency fallback + migration path) that a field seller can use in a 10–12 minute discovery/demo conversation. Keep it light, repeatable, and engineer-friendly for follow-up.

Audience and persona focus:
- Primary: Integration engineers / platform engineers at mid-market SaaS (50–500 engs) evaluating inference for chat/agent features.
- Secondary: Product managers and solutions architects who will influence purchase.
- Technical constraints we expect to see: token budgets, latency targets (<150ms for short responses, <400ms for longer threads), data residency requirements.

Sprint hypotheses (what we want to learn):
1) A three-step story (value -> predictable economics -> fallback controls) improves buyer confidence in 10–15m calls vs a product tour.
2) A single reference demo (embed + cache + fallback) reduces pilot friction and shortens technical qualification by 30%.
3) Sellers armed with a tiny config snippet + canary checklist will get customers to agree to a 2-week pilot more often.

Core story arc (3 slides):
- Slide A: "What predictable inference means" (one-sentence opener + 2 metrics)
  - 1-liner: "Ship LLM features without surprise bills or outages."
  - Metrics: median token cost, p50 latency, baseline throughput for a 4-node dedicated pool.
  - Speaker note: use a real example — e.g., customer X moved from ad-hoc endpoints to reserved capacity and cut per-request cost by ~40% (anonymized numbers).

- Slide B: "Controls that keep you in control" (ops knobs + brief demo flow)
  - Bullets: routing policies, autoscale cap, kv/prefix caching, quantization profiles, graceful fallbacks.
  - Mini-diagram (verbally): flow for request -> router -> model tier A/B -> fallback to cheaper variant -> degrade gracefully.
  - Speaker note: call out the three levers sellers should surface: latency SLO, cost cap, and data isolation needs.

- Slide C: "Pilot to production path" (pilot success criteria + handoff checklist)
  - Pilot success metrics (agree with buyer): 95th percentile latency target, cost per 1k tokens, 2 sample prompts with fidelity threshold.
  - Handoff checklist: onboarding API key, model/version pin, canary route config, observability hooks enabled.
  - Speaker note: ask for a 2-week pilot with a mutually agreed sample set.

Quick demo script (6–8 minutes):
- 0:00–1:00: one-sentence problem + who we help
- 1:00–2:00: Slide A walkthrough (numbers + example)
- 2:00–4:00: Demo of a single endpoint responding to a 3-turn thread, show token usage and latency via console (live or recorded clip)
- 4:00–5:30: Slide B (explain fallback and cost controls) — show config snippet for routing policy
- 5:30–6:30: Slide C + ask for pilot (confirm success criteria)

Objection handling (quick lines):
- "We already have endpoints": "Great — what are your 95th % latency and per-token costs today? We usually start pilots where those are measurable and show predictable unit economics with autoscale offload for spikes."
- "Security/compliance concerns": "We can run a private deployment (VPC/on-prem) with KMS/HSM integrations; we’ll include audit log hooks in the pilot scope."
- "Model fidelity worries": "We pin a model variant and run sample prompts pre-pilot — if the sample fails, we iterate model or prompt before committing."

Technical appendix (copyable snippets for sellers):
- Minimal config to propose in a pilot (one-liner + 3 keys sellers can paste):
  - model: v1-relevant-llama-quant
  - routing_policy: prefer_dedicated_then_hosted
  - autoscale: min_replicas:1, max_replicas:4, burst: 2
  - cache_profile: small_prefix_kv

- Canary checklist (engineers):
  - verify pin/version in request header (X-Model-Version)
  - enable token-breakdown traces for route under test
  - memory/kv cache warming: send 50 warm-up requests for typical prompt shapes
  - failure mode: set fallback_variant to smaller model with response_suppression:low

KPIs to track during pilot:
- Business: conversion from pilot -> paid (target 40%), time-to-first-meaningful-metric (days), product usage delta when feature enabled.
- Technical: p95 latency, median tokens per response, cost per 1k tokens, #fallbacks per 1k requests.

Notes-to-self / rough tactical ideas (informal):
- Try a short animated gif showing a request falling back to cheaper variant — simple visual sells.
- Record two short console clips: 1) hosted fast response, 2) dedicated pool under load showing stable latency. Use both depending on buyer tier.
- Bake a 'pilot pack' repo: README + sample dataset + 1-click config for a sandbox. Link during follow-up.
- Consider a micro-deck variant for platform engineers (strip business slides, keep technical flows).

Open questions / follow-ups for the sprint:
1) Can we get anonymized cost/latency stats from two existing customers to use as examples? (ask PMs).
2) Is there a one-liner legal/SD k-format for VPC/on-prem that sellers can drop in an email?
3) Who owns the pilot pack repo? assign to solutions-eng.

Next steps (this week):
- [ ] Maya: draft the 3-slide deck + 2 demo clips (due Thu)
- [ ] Aarav: scaffold the pilot pack repo + example dataset (due Fri)
- [ ] Samira: reach out to two reference customers for anonymized metrics (due Mon)
- [ ] Diego: create a short seller-facing email template with the short ask and pilot success criteria (due Fri)

Appendix: quick email template (seller -> buyer) — keep it short
Subject: 2-week pilot to validate [feature] latency & cost
Hi [Name],
Thanks for chatting earlier — we can run a two-week pilot that demonstrates latency and predictable token economics for your [feature]. Proposal: agree on 2 test prompts, a p95 latency target, and cost cap. We’ll share a small sandbox and a one-line config to get you started.
If that sounds useful I’ll send the pilot pack and schedule a 30-min kickoff.
Best, Maya

End of draft — notes intentionally informal. This is meant to be an experimental, low-friction seller artifact. Save as "draft" until we get two customer metrics to cite and a 30s gif for Slide B.
